subject: english-literature
title: Marlowe's Renaissance Bargain: Knowledge and Damnation
welcome_lead: Enter Christopher Marlowe's c.1592 tragedy and trace how Renaissance humanism, medieval morality and Reformation theology converge on Faustus's contract.
meta_desc: A-Level adventure on Marlowe's Doctor Faustus: Renaissance humanism, morality play heritage, and Calvinist damnation.
final_note: Faustus signs a contract he could have torn up at any moment. Marlowe leaves us asking why repentance keeps not coming.

walkthroughs.body_html: Christopher Marlowe (1564–1593) was Shakespeare's exact contemporary, -educated, and possibly an intelligence operative. Doctor Faustus was likely written c.1588–1592 and performed by the Admiral's Men. It draws on the anonymous English Faust Book (1592 translation of the German Historia von D. Johann Fausten, 1587). Marlowe was killed in Deptford in May 1593 in disputed circumstances; the play's print history is correspondingly tangled.

The play retains morality-play machinery — Good and Bad Angels, Seven Deadly Sins, Old Man — but locates them within a tragic protagonist of psychological depth. Marlowe converts allegorical figures into externalisations of Faustus's interiority. The result is hybrid: medieval form, Renaissance consciousness. Critics including Helen Cooper trace this transitional poetics; AO3 responses gain from naming this hybridity precisely.

Faustus repeatedly considers repentance ('Yet, Faustus, call on God') but cannot complete the gesture. Critics including Pauline Honderich and John Stachniewski read this as Calvinist dramaturgy: Faustus is reprobate, his repentance theatrically performed but soteriologically null. Other critics (Edward Snow) emphasise his agency and intellectual stubbornness. AO5 rewards engagement with both lenses.

mcqs.q: What is the dramatic function of a soliloquy?
options: A soliloquy is any long speech a character gives.
It reveals a character's inner thoughts directly to the audience while the character is alone on stage — a convention granting access to private psychology.
Postmodernism means writing about the future.
A soliloquy is when characters argue with each other.
The narrator and author are different words for the same thing.
Postmodernism just means literature written after modernism.
Postmodernism means writing about the future.
Self-aware metafiction, intertextuality, scepticism toward grand narratives, playfulness with form, and blurring of high/low culture.

mcqs.q: Why must students distinguish the narrator from the author?
options: The narrator is a constructed voice within the text; the author is the real person who created it. Conflating them misreads irony, unreliable narration and persona.
Postmodernism means writing about the future.
The narrator and author are different words for the same thing.
The narrator's views are always the author's views.
